title: 2007 AMC 10A Problem 11
statement: The numbers from \(1\) to \(8\) are placed at the vertices of a cube in such a manner that the sum of the four numbers on each face is the same. What is this common sum?

solutions.text:
Each vertex belongs to exactly three faces, so summing the numbers over all six faces gives \[ \begin{aligned} 3(1 + 2 + \cdots + 8) &= 3 \cdot 36 \\ &= 108. \end{aligned} \]

There are six faces, so the common sum is \(108 \div 6 = 18.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Each vertex of a cube lies on exactly three faces
Adding all six face sums counts each vertex \(3\) times: \(3(1 + 2 + \cdots + 8)\)
